name: go-github-policy-governed-redirect-resolution
instr:
go-github cannot govern redirects with policies or expose ordered redirect evidence across downloads, archives, migrations, repository redirects, and dependency snapshots. Implement client-wide and request-local policies without coupling cloned clients or concurrent requests. Preserve existing results, rate behavior, headers, response metadata, body ownership, endpoint paths, archive options, preview headers, direct bodies, external streaming ownership, and legacy URL, Response, string, body, and error observations.

Record every attempted hop in network order with its source, resolved target, status, and zero-based index, plus the terminal URL and Response evidence. Policy rejection, cycles, and exhausted hop limits must stop before contacting the disallowed target and return the completed trace. Keep malformed locations, cancellation, and transport failures distinguishable. Never forward GitHub authorization or one-time-password credentials across origins.

`NewClient` must expose the four services named below through `Client.Actions`, `Client.Repositories`, `Client.Migrations`, and `Client.DependencyGraph`. Their governed entry points must share policy, tracing, limits, authentication boundaries, and failure classification. Organization migration resolution returns a deterministic terminal error and empty completed trace when no redirect exists. User migration resolution stays request-local and never mutates the shared HTTP client's `CheckRedirect`.
